newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesians evacuated after volcano spews hot gas.
newsitem.headline: Indonesians evacuated after volcano spews hot gas.

text.p: Thousands of Indonesian villagers living near Mount Merapi in Central Java were evacuated on Friday as a precaution after the volcano spewed hot gas, a vulcanology official said.

"The volcano spewed hot gases today. Thousands of people living near Merapi have been evacuated because we don't want to take any risks," the official at the vulcanology office in Yogyakarta told Reuters by telephone.
The official, who declined to give other details, said villagers were evacuated because the hot gas moved towards a number of villages.
He said said the office continued to monitor the volcano, which has been expelling hot lava and ash this week.
The 2,911-metre (9,548 ft) Merapi erupted without warning in November 1994, killing 60 people and displacing more than 2,000 from its fertile slopes, 400 km (250 miles) east of Jakarta.

Villagers living near Merapi had been told to be ready to evacuate because of the volcano's recent intensified activities. Residents of Turgo and Tritis villages, which were badly affected by the 1994 eruption, had earlier been asked to stay in a nearby school.

It is a common practice during times of high volcanic activity for people from the most vulnerable villages to sleep in designated evacuation centres at night to ensure they could be moved quickly in case of an eruption.
Merapi, Indonesia's most active volcano, recorded its most destructive eruption this century in 1930, when 1,300 people were killed.
